d: Nord Anglia International School Abu Dhabi is seeking a forward-thinking, creative, and innovative English Teacher to join our high-performing secondary team.
The start date for this position is January 2027.

At Nord Anglia Education, our schools shape a generation of creative and resilient global citizens who leave our schools with everything they need for success – whatever they choose to be or do in life. When it comes to creating memorable learning experiences both within and beyond our classrooms, our family of more than 13,000 passionate staff are experts in their academic and commercial professions and play a vital role in the world-class experience our schools provide.

We educate more than 74,000 children in 32 countries, our 84 schools in the Middle East, the Americas, Europe and Asia form our diverse global family, making us the largest provider of premium education in the world.

Nord Anglia International School Abu Dhabi – described recently in Yalla Magazine as the school to watch out for – is a forward-thinking, innovative school whose mission is to Lead the Way, inspiring everyone to be extraordinary. Located on Al Reem Island, our purpose-built campus brings together talented educators and professionals who share a commitment to making everyday count. NAS Abu Dhabi is a place where people feel valued and supported to do their best work.

We build a culture of support, collaboration, respect and continuous growth. Everyone here plays a part in shaping a positive environment where staff, students and their families can thrive. As part of Nord Anglia Education, our team benefits from global expertise, professional learning opportunities, and the shared purpose of preparing young people for their future in an ever-changing world.

All our students – from Early Years Foundation Stage through to IGCSEs and A-levels – follow the English National Curriculum. The successful candidate will be able to inspire students of all ages and abilities. Classroom resources are plentiful, and expectations are high for achievement for all students. Building and maintaining positive relationships with parents is essential and is a key part of maximising student progress.
More detail about the role and requirements can be found in the accompanying job description. - Secondary Subject Teacher - NASAD JD.pdf
q: You will be a teacher who is passionate about their profession and seeks continuous improvement. You will have a positive mindset and will always do your very best for students, for parents and for colleagues. You will have strong experience of the UK national curriculum; further experience of international education will be an added advantage.

You will be an excellent communicator who will work well with all members of the community. You will have a strong focus on being the best teacher you can be and will also participate fully in the extra-curricular aspects of school life. You will be responsible for encouraging and developing further our culture of inspiration, enjoyment and success. Keen to collaborate and share your expertise, you will have good interpersonal skills and the ability and confidence to build strong working relationships. The flexibility and open-mindedness required to adapt quickly to a fast-paced international environment are essential.
Applicants should submit a CV, letter of application and the details of two professional referees, one of which should be your current Line Manager.

At Nord Anglia Education we are committed to providing a world class, safe, happy environment in which children and young people are able to thrive and learn. We are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of all our pupils irrespective of race, ability, religion, gender or culture.

d: The role is responsible to keeps credit, capital, liquidity and operational risk within the Board-approved risk appetite and in line with the CBB Rulebook. It leads the end-to-end credit risk function, combining strategic oversight with hands-on, techno-functional work in data analytics, credit decision engine management and model development.
q: Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Mathematics, Statistics, Risk Management or a related field; a Master's degree is preferred.
A recognized risk or finance certification, such as FRM, PRM, CFA or ACCA/CPA, is preferred.
At least 10 years in risk management within banking or financial services, including at least 8 years in credit risk and at least 5 years in a senior role.
Hands-on experience in retail or consumer credit risk, ideally covering microfinance, BNPL or credit cards in Bahrain or the GCC.
Proven experience with credit decision engines, scorecards and credit risk models.
Working knowledge of the CBB Rulebook, regulatory reporting obligations, ICAAP, capital adequacy and liquidity requirements.
Experience with IFRS 9 ECL methodology and stress testing.
Experience presenting to Boards, Board committees, regulators and investors.
r: Design, maintain and review at least annually the ERM Framework and Risk Appetite Statement, for ExCom review and Board approval; report material changes to the Board.
Own the Risk Management policy suite and keep it aligned with CBB Rulebook requirements and changes.
Maintain the enterprise risk register and Key Risk Indicators (KRIs), with tolerance thresholds and escalation triggers.
Provide independent risk sign-off on new products, pricing changes, material business decisions and material variations to the scope of the CBB licence.
Advise senior management on the risk implications of strategy and business decisions across microfinancing, BNPL and credit cards.
Promote a sound risk culture through training and awareness across the three lines of defence.
Own the credit risk management framework, including product-level credit policies for microfinancing, BNPL and credit cards, scoring and decisioning criteria, credit limits and approval authorities.
Set loan-size and tenor grids by customer segment, consistent with the Board-approved risk appetite.
Review the portfolio's risk indicators daily, including delinquency, arrears, roll rates and early-warning signals.
Set and monitor portfolio quality metrics (PAR, NPL, default and delinquency rates, roll rates, vintage curves) against approved targets and market benchmarks, and escalate breaches proactively.
Monitor concentration risk by segment, product, merchant and counterparty, and advise on collections strategy.
Oversee provisioning and impairment under the IFRS 9 expected credit loss (ECL) methodology, including staging criteria, model assumptions and management overlays, in coordination with Finance.
Monitor and report exposures to controllers and close links, ensuring compliance with limits and tracking related action plans.
Keep the credit decision engine and its scorecards and rules up to date with current risk appetite and market conditions.
Coordinate periodic recalibration, back-testing and validation of decisioning rules and credit scoring models.
Work with IT and vendors to implement decision engine changes, with version control and a full audit trail of every rule change.
Build, test and refine credit risk and scoring models for accuracy, stability and predictive power.
Stay hands-on with database queries, data extraction and dataset preparation for analysis.
Run ongoing analytics to detect emerging risk trends, anomalies and early portfolio deterioration, and turn findings into actions for underwriting, collections and portfolio strategy.
Work with IT and Data teams to source additional data (credit bureau, alternative data, internal transactional data) to strengthen decisioning.
Define customer segments by risk profile, behaviour and profitability to support targeted credit strategies.
Develop segment-specific underwriting criteria and provide risk input into pricing and product design, to grow the portfolio responsibly.
Partner with Sales, Marketing and Product to identify growth opportunities within approved risk parameters, while keeping the independence of the risk function.
Oversee the Internal Capital Adequacy Assessment Process (ICAAP) and monitor compliance with CBB capital adequacy requirements (Module CA), including the gearing ratio.
Monitor compliance with minimum liquidity requirements and maintain the approved liquidity management and contingency funding policy.
Run periodic stress testing and scenario analysis covering credit losses, funding and liquidity stress, and macroeconomic shocks; report results and recommended actions.
Own operational risk management, including risk and control self-assessments (RCSAs), incident and loss-event reporting, and root-cause follow-up.
Identify and mitigate operational risks across the credit lifecycle: origination, disbursement, monitoring and collections.
Ensure credit operations comply with internal policies, CBB regulations, and AML/CFT and consumer protection requirements.
Oversee business continuity management, and monitor fraud, outsourcing/third-party and technology risk in coordination with the relevant functions.

Present regular risk reports to the CEO, the ACGC, the Board Risk Committee (where constituted) and the Board, covering risk appetite adherence, KRIs, portfolio performance, capital, liquidity, emerging risks and key decisions.

Act as the key point of contact with the CBB on risk matters: attend CBB meetings, respond promptly to information requests, and prepare and submit accurate, timely credit risk, portfolio and other required regulatory reports.
Prepare credit risk and portfolio performance reports for investors and shareholders, supporting fundraising and governance requirements.
Work with Compliance and the MLRO on financial-crime risk indicators embedded in lending and card products.
Support internal and external audits and CBB inspections, and track remediation of risk-related findings to closure.

d: FlyAkeed is an innovative online platform focused on transforming the travel booking experience by enabling seamless flight and hotel reservations. Established in 2017 and headquartered in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, we aim to simplify work-related travel planning for businesses and individuals alike.
FlyAkeed is proudly backed by notable investors including PIF subsidiary Sanabil Investments, Elm, Artal Capital, and Alrajhi Partners.

The Senior Customer Onboarding manages the onboarding journey for new customers, ensuring their business requirements, account information, user access, and operational setup are completed accurately and on time. The role serves as a key point of contact for customers and internal teams, helping accelerate customer activation and deliver a smooth onboarding experience.
q: Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Tourism, Hospitality, or a related field.
Experience in customer onboarding, customer success, account coordination, or operations.
Strong coordination, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
High attention to detail and ability to manage documentation and multiple customer onboarding cases.
Comfortable working with digital platforms, spreadsheets, and CRM or customer management systems.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English; Arabic is an advantage.
r: Manage the end-to-end onboarding process for new customers, from initial handover through account activation.
Guide customers through registration, account setup, required documentation, and implementation steps.
Understand customer requirements and coordinate the configuration of accounts, user access, and platform settings.
Coordinate with Sales, Account Management, Product, Technology, Finance, and Operations to complete onboarding requirements.
Deliver platform walkthroughs and training to help customers and their users adopt FlyAkeed’s services effectively.
Track onboarding progress, identify blockers, and proactively follow up to ensure timely activation.
Provide onboarding support, respond to customer queries, and coordinate the resolution of initial setup issues.
Maintain accurate customer onboarding records, trackers, and performance reports.
Identify recurring onboarding challenges and recommend improvements to processes, guidance, and customer communications.
Support the development of onboarding materials, templates, and standard operating procedures.
Provide guidance and knowledge-sharing to other team members as needed.
